newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dickson could up Barney's bid if needed.
newsitem.headline: Dickson could up Barney's bid if needed.

text.p: Barney's Inc offers Dickson Concepts International Ltd a unique chance to enter the U.S. luxury market and the Hong Kong retailer may therefore be willing to pay a higher price to achieve that, analysts said.

Dickson Concepts has offered to buy Barney's for US$240 million and a minority interest in Barney's non-U.S. store licensing income, but Barney's official committee of unsecured creditors rejected the offer on Tuesday.
"I personally believe Dickson will raise the bid (if necessary). It offers a good chance for them to enter the U.S. market," said Louisa Sung, retail analyst at Sassoon Securities.
"Dickson wants to go international and it doesn't have a presence in the U.S. and more important is Barney's upmarket image matches Dickson's business strategy," she said.
Barney's unsecured creditors said the value of the company was substantially higher than Dickson's proposal. Market estimates have put the value at around US$350 million.
Elizabeth Gouw, an analyst at UBS Securities, said she was not surprised by the committee's response.

"Dickson seems keen to bid for Barney's because it has plenty of cash on hand. If it misses this opportunity, it may not find another company that could give it the same kind of presence in the U.S.," she added.
Dickson's chairman Dickson Poon said last week the company's cash position was HK$1.3 billion. Analysts estimated the figure would grow to HK$1.4 billion by the end of 1997.
Dickson might raise its bid by offering US$300 million in cash plus a minority interest in non-U.S. licensing, Hong Kong analysts said.
"It's their strategy to start from a low price," one analyst at a regional house said.
Barney's, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection last year, has said it was talking with at least three potential investors, including Dickson.
Saks Holdings Inc previously expressed interest in the company and Neiman Marcus Group Inc has been cited by industry experts as a potential bidder.
Barney's was expected to take 10 days to two weeks to reach a decision on Dickson's proposal, the analyst at the regional house said.
The bid would also need the approval of the U.S. bankruptcy court. Poon said it could take between four and eight months for the company to secure the required approvals for the purchase.
If the bid is successful, Dickson could take at least three years to turn Barney's around, Sassoon's Sung said. "This will greatly stretch Dickson's profits."
Barney's reported sales of US$366 million (HK$2.83 billion) for the 53 weeks to August 3, 1996.
Dickson Concepts reported turnover of HK$3.94 billion for the year ended March 31, 1996.
